column2: Equivalent: change_log rows are keyed by (mailbox_id, seq) and the seq comes from the t.seq column of the unnest, never from insertion order; the mailbox row is locked FOR UPDATE first, so no concurrent writer shares the (mailbox, seq) range, and every read (CHANGES) orders by seq. The physical order of the insert is unobservable through the repository.

Redundant second line of defence: lock_blobs builds a BTreeMap, so the arrays bound to the statement are already ascending and the SQL ORDER BY cannot change the lock order for any reachable input. The forced-crossing knob tests do NOT kill it (that knob replaces the whole path); blob_lock_order_matrix_has_no_deadlock_and_exact_refcounts exercises the production path with rotated and reversed inputs and would notice a lost ordering only if the BTreeMap were also removed. Gap: nothing mutates the BTreeMap itself (PG8 carry-over).

Presence-pinned only: no statement of the codebase filters on (mailbox_id, thread_id) (thread ids are only read back as a column, the lookup by Message-ID uses messages_msgid), so there is no query whose plan could pin it. It is pinned by the catalog snapshot and by the sqlite_master structure oracle (oracle column: yes). Kept for the planned JMAP thread queries; a plan test belongs with the first statement that uses it.
